body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students solve adding-to, taking-from and putting-together story problems within 20 using drawings, objects and number sentences (1.OA.A.1).
- Students relate counting to addition and subtraction by counting on and counting back (1.OA.C.5).
- Students add and subtract within 20 using counting on and other strategies, building fluency within 10 (1.OA.C.6).

MATERIALS
- Counters (or small snacks, buttons or bottle caps from the class counting collections)
- A number path or number line from 0 to 20 for each student
- Ten frames (two per student, to show numbers to 20)
- Whiteboards and markers, or tablets with the class activities open for photos of work

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Story Problems together. Act out a story with students as birds: 12 birds on a tree (12 students stand), 4 fly away (4 sit). How many are left? Write 12 - 4 = 8 together.
Day 2: Lesson activity: Count On, Count Back. Model on the number path: start at 8, hop 3 to 11. Students try each question with the number path, then tell a partner why we start with the bigger number.
Day 3: Apple Orchard Story Problems. Read each story aloud twice. Students solve with counters or drawings and write a number sentence; photograph or draw their work.
Day 4: Make Your Own Story Problem. Model one about the class pet or lunch. Students draw and record their own story, then trade with a partner to solve.
Day 5: Assessment: Adding and Taking Away Check. Read each problem aloud. Students work alone with counters and number paths available. Note who counts all and who counts on.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: keep numbers within 10 at first (6 apples and 3 more), and let students act out the story with counters before drawing it.
- Support: give a number sentence frame with boxes (__ + __ = __) to fill in.
- Stretch: offer change-unknown stories (Bear had 8 apples. She picked some more. Now she has 13. How many did she pick?) and ask for two different ways to solve one problem.
- Multilingual learners: pre-teach story words with pictures and gestures: more, left, in all, fly away, picks. Act each one out. Let students tell their own story problem in their home language first.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This month we are solving story problems by drawing pictures, using counters, and counting on. You can make up story problems at home: "You have 7 grapes. I give you 4 more. How many now?" Ask your child to show you how they figured it out. Counting on from the bigger number (7... 8, 9, 10, 11) is a great strategy to praise.
title: Teacher guide: Adding and Taking Away Within 20
